clue.text: Camp entertainer is an old soldier

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a host at a Butlin's holiday camp, who wears a red jacket
second meaning: a British infantryman of past centuries in a scarlet tunic

explanation.surface: A holiday-camp entertainer turns out to be a former army man.
explanation.walkthrough: Butlin's is a chain of British holiday camps whose entertainers are known by their red jackets.
explanation.definitionFit: The same word names both the uniformed Butlin's staff and the historic British infantryman, each named for the red jacket.

clue.text: Flipping heavy book: Vulcan's expressing feelings

indicators.note: flipping something over turns it the other way, so the word for a book is read backwards

parts.note: a tome is a large weighty volume
the setter speaking of himself: Vulcan has, I've

explanation.surface: A setter boasts of hurling a big book in a show of temper.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter's pseudonym stands for 'I', so Vulcan's becomes I'VE.
explanation.definitionFit: Emotive language is charged with emotion, conveying or stirring up feelings.

clue.text: He takes a bow, promoted in police department

indicators.note: in says one piece is placed inside the department's letters

parts.note: the Criminal Investigation Department
someone promoted has moved up

explanation.surface: A detective takes a bow after moving up the ranks in his department.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Takes a bow' sounds like acknowledging applause; it means carries a bow and arrow. CID is the British detective branch.
explanation.definitionFit: The Roman love god is pictured as an archer carrying a bow with which he shoots his arrows.

clue.text: Very old canine tooth's first to disintegrate

indicators.note: falling to pieces means the letters come apart and regroup in a new order

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: first asks only for the opening letter of the word tooth

parts.note: the opening letter of tooth

explanation.surface: An elderly dog's fang is starting to crumble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Canine tooth' reads as one dental phrase, but canine is fodder and tooth only supplies its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Ancient describes something belonging to the distant past, a direct synonym of extremely old.

clue.text: Rage at seducer, a bloodsucker

parts.note: a vamp is a woman who seduces men
ire is anger

explanation.surface: Someone fumes at a seducer who exploits people.
explanation.walkthrough: The rage word is placed at the end of the seducer word, so the pieces join in the reverse of clue order.
explanation.definitionFit: A vampire is the legendary creature that feeds on human blood.

clue.text: A uniform required for exam?

parts.note: taken as written
level means even, the same throughout

explanation.surface: Is a school uniform needed to sit an exam?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Uniform' suggests school clothes but is an adjective meaning even. A-levels are the exams English pupils take at about 18.
explanation.definitionFit: An A-level is the advanced school-leaving examination in England, Wales and Northern Ireland.

clue.text: Noble not turning up for university

parts.note: a prince is a nobleman

indicators.note: in a down entry, turning up means the word reads from bottom to top

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A nobleman fails to arrive at college.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not turning up' reads as absence, but it is the word not reversed.
explanation.definitionFit: Princeton is an Ivy League university in New Jersey.

clue.text: Chirpy types heading off youthful disease

indicators.note: heading off says the head, the first letter, is taken away

parts.note: crickets are insects that chirp

explanation.surface: Cheerful people go off to fight a childhood illness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chirpy' suggests cheerful people; it means insects that chirp.
explanation.definitionFit: Rickets is a bone-softening condition caused by vitamin D deficiency, chiefly affecting children.

clue.text: Site of imperial palaces in Bedford, remarkably big town

indicators.note: remarkably suggests something done in an unusual way, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
a city is a large town

explanation.surface: A remarkably big English town is said to house royal palaces.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' looks like a link to Bedford, an English county town, but it is part of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: The Forbidden City in Beijing was the palace complex of the Chinese emperors.

clue.text: Band shortening housework

indicators.note: shortening cuts each word down to its abbreviated form

parts.note: one printed word that the wordplay reads as two, house and work
HO is the standard short form of house
op, short for opus, is a work

explanation.surface: A musical group's chores are being cut down.
explanation.walkthrough: Housework is read as two words, house and work, each cut to its usual abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A hoop is a circular band, such as the metal ring around a barrel.

clue.text: How to secure a little garlic?

definitions.text: How to secure a little garlic?

parts.note: a clove is one segment of a garlic bulb
to hitch is to fasten with a rope

explanation.surface: A kitchen question about fastening a small portion of garlic.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also defines the answer: a knot is literally a way to secure something, and its name is a bit of garlic plus a word for fastening.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a common knot of two half hitches used to fasten a rope to a post, so it is a way to secure things.

clue.text: Arouse reader

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to stir up a feeling, or to set alight
second meaning: Amazon's e-book reading device

explanation.walkthrough: The two words look like a phrase about exciting a reader, but each defines the answer separately.
explanation.definitionFit: To kindle interest is to arouse it, and the Kindle is Amazon's electronic book device.

clue.text: Stranded across lake, turned white

indicators.note: across means one word stretches over the other, holding it inside

parts.note: a beached boat or whale is stranded on shore
L is the abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: Someone stuck on the far side of a lake has gone pale.
explanation.definitionFit: Bleached means lost colour or made white, as by sun or chemicals.

clue.text: Buzz off, dude — head off for bliss

indicators.note: with its head off, the word loses its first letter

parts.note: beat it is slang for go away
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone tells a man to clear off, then go off in search of happiness.
explanation.definitionFit: Beatitude is supreme blessedness or happiness, a state of perfect bliss.

clue.text: Being aggressively smashed in Hull?

parts.note: surface reading: getting violently drunk, or attacked, in the Yorkshire city of Hull
setter's reading: a ship's hull is struck and broken open by an underwater weapon

explanation.walkthrough: The capital H makes Hull the English port city, but the clue means a ship's body hit below the waterline.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship struck by a self-propelled underwater missile has its hull blasted open.

clue.text: Secret police in almost unmoving position

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: stasis is a state of standing still

explanation.surface: Secret police officers stand nearly motionless on watch.
explanation.definitionFit: The Stasi was the state security service of communist East Germany.

clue.text: Nasty mark on end of toe is a big worry

parts.note: a scar is a mark left by a wound

indicators.note: end of picks out just the final letter of the following word

parts.note: the final letter of toe

explanation.surface: A wound on the tip of one's toe is alarming.
explanation.definitionFit: A scare is a fright or a widespread alarm, a sudden cause for serious concern.

clue.text: Victor avoiding hot pink flower

indicators.note: avoiding says the letter for the next word is kept out

parts.note: a champion is a winner
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: A winner steers clear of a fiery pink bloom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Victor' might be the V of the NATO alphabet, but here it is a winner.
explanation.definitionFit: Campion is a wildflower, the red campion bearing pink blooms.

clue.text: Can enter amazing year, a notable one

indicators.note: amazing suggests something astonishing, a signal to mix up the letters

parts.note: taken as written
Y is the abbreviation for year

explanation.surface: Someone may sign up for a remarkable twelve months.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One' refers back to year: the answer is a notable kind of year.
explanation.definitionFit: A centenary is a hundredth anniversary, a year singled out for celebration.

clue.text: Pub, a place for souvlaki and retsina?

parts.note: a tavern is an inn or pub
taken as written

explanation.surface: Asking whether a bar is somewhere to get Greek kebabs and wine.
explanation.walkthrough: Souvlaki are Greek grilled meat skewers and retsina is Greek resinated wine; the question mark admits the definition is by example.
explanation.definitionFit: A taverna is a small Greek restaurant, the typical setting for those dishes and drinks.

clue.text: Dishonestly manipulating tackle

definitions.meaning: first meaning: fixing a result by fraud
second meaning: a ship's ropes and gear

explanation.walkthrough: 'Tackle' suggests a foul in sport, but it is the noun for a ship's gear.
explanation.definitionFit: Rigging is both the act of fixing something fraudulently and the system of ropes supporting a ship's masts.

clue.text: I'd raised short magic formula to cause disappearance

indicators.note: in a down entry, raised means read upwards, from bottom to top

parts.note: taken as written, without the apostrophe

indicators.note: short means the word is cut off before its last letter

parts.note: a spell is an incantation

explanation.surface: A conjuror claims to have lifted a brief incantation to make things vanish.
explanation.definitionFit: To dispel is to drive away or make vanish, as doubts or fears are dispelled.

clue.text: One struggling to recall a cinema's collapse

indicators.note: something that collapses falls into a heap, so the letters are reassembled differently

parts.note: taken as written, without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: Someone tries hard to remember when a picture house fell down.
explanation.definitionFit: An amnesiac suffers from memory loss and so has difficulty remembering things.

clue.text: Countenance decline in struggle

indicators.note: in says the first word is placed inside the second

parts.note: to vie is to compete
to sag is to droop or fall

explanation.surface: Someone refuses to accept a downturn while fighting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Countenance' looks like a verb meaning permit; it is the noun for a face.
explanation.definitionFit: A visage is a person's face, and countenance is a literary word for the face.

clue.text: Father with new alluring woman

parts.note: to sire is to father; a sire is a male parent
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: A dad turns up with a fresh, attractive partner.
explanation.definitionFit: A siren is a seductive woman, after the mythical singers who lured sailors to their doom.

clue.text: Man that's simple and safe as a disciple

parts.note: Simple Simon is the nursery-rhyme simpleton
peter is old criminal slang for a safe

explanation.surface: A naive and reliable man is taken on as a follower.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Safe' reads as an adjective meaning trustworthy, but it is the noun: a safe-breaker is a peterman.
explanation.definitionFit: Simon Peter is the full name of the apostle Peter, one of Jesus's twelve disciples.

clue.text: Attack drawer with papers

parts.note: an RA, a Royal Academician, is an artist who draws
ID means identity papers

explanation.surface: Someone goes for a chest of drawers full of documents.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drawer' looks like part of a desk, but it is one who draws, an artist.
explanation.definitionFit: A raid is a sudden assault on a place, by soldiers or police.

clue.text: Mockingly say led inside, returning stripped

indicators.note: returning means going back, so the letters are read in the opposite direction
stripped means the outer letters of the phrase are removed, leaving a run from inside

parts.note: the letters from the end of say to the start of inside

explanation.surface: A sneering remark about someone escorted indoors, coming back with no clothes on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Inside' looks like the hiding signal but is part of the run of letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Snidely means in a sneering, slyly disparaging way, much like mockingly.

clue.text: Rage can break out, leading to mass slaughter

indicators.note: breaking out suggests escaping in disorder, so the letters scatter and regroup

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Anger may erupt and end in bloodshed.
explanation.definitionFit: Carnage is the killing of large numbers of people, a bloodbath.
